---
title: "A top five that changes members"
description: "A ranking animation where countries join and leave the top five: marks matched across years slide to their new rank, and marks present in only one year fade in or out."
categories: [Animation]
image: figs/ranking-enter-exit-poster.png
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
```

[The bar chart race](bar-race.qmd) follows the same ten countries through every year.
A real league table is less tidy: the top five of 1952 is not the top five of 2007, so
some bars have nowhere to come from and others nowhere to go. The tween handles both
cases with one rule. A bar found in two adjacent years moves from one to the other; a
bar found in only one of them fades in or out on the spot.

```{r}
library(gapminder)

eu <- as.data.frame(gapminder[gapminder$continent == "Europe", ])
top5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(eu, eu$year), function(d) {
  d <- head(d[order(-d$gdpPercap), ], 5)
  d$rank <- 1:5
  d
}))

table(top5$country)
```

Ten countries pass through Europe's top five by GDP per capita over the twelve
survey years. Norway and Switzerland are in every year; Sweden appears once.

```{r}
a <- vplot(top5, width = 7, height = 3.6) |>
  mark_bar(x = 6 - rank, y = gdpPercap, fill = country) |>
  mark_text(x = 6 - rank, y = gdpPercap + 600, label = country,
            hjust = 0, size = 10) |>
  coord_flip() |>
  guides(fill = "none") |>
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 60000)) |>
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) |>
  labs(title = "Europe's five highest GDPs per capita, {closest_state}",
       x = NULL, y = "GDP per capita (1990 dollars)") |>
  transition_states(year, transition_length = 2, state_length = 1, wrap = FALSE) |>
  animate(nframes = 330, fps = 25)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
dir.create("figs", showWarnings = FALSE)
anim_save("figs/ranking-enter-exit.svg", a)
# The gallery card: the animation's own last frame.
anim_frame("figs/ranking-enter-exit-poster.png", a, scale = 100 / a@dpi)
knitr::include_graphics("figs/ranking-enter-exit.svg")
```

Watch the bottom slots. The United Kingdom is third in 1952 and gone after 1957.
Germany comes in in 1962, drops out for Sweden's single year in 1967 and is back in
1972. On the move from 1967 to 1972 the leaver and the newcomer hold the same slot,
fifth, so for the length of the move two bars share it, one fading out while the other
fades in. Iceland and Austria come and go in the 1980s and 1990s, and Ireland arrives
in third place in 2002 and climbs to second.

## How bars are matched

Each bar is keyed by its group, and with no `group` or `data_id` the group is the
combination of the layer's discrete mappings, here `fill = country` (the labels are
keyed by `label = country`). So the engine looks for the same country in the next
year:

- **found**: the bar slides from its old rank to its new one and its length tweens;
- **missing from the next year**: the bar fades out where it is;
- **missing from the previous year**: the bar fades in at its new place.

The fade runs on the alpha easing, so `ease_aes(alpha = ...)` shapes it separately from
the movement. Because the scales are trained once over all the years, a country that
enters gets the same colour and is measured against the same axis as everyone else.

One detail in the data matters: the axis is extended to 60 000 so the labels to the
right of the longest bar stay inside the panel. `eu$country` can stay a factor: the
colour scale drops the levels no row uses, as in ggplot2, so it only knows the ten
countries that appear rather than all 142 levels of `gapminder$country`.
